messages:
maria: Heads up — Support just escalated a major latency regression for customer acme-inc. p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~850ms over the last 30m, p99 spiking to ~2s. They see it on the /v1/generate endpoint in us-west.

support-ops: reported via ticket #INC-5412 — linking metrics: https://grafana.redwood/acme-inc/requests?panel=latency (they pasted a screenshot). Also they attached curl repro and said it repros consistently during their load test.

jamal: checking logs now. noticing increased queueing on the runtime side. A lot of requests hitting model-redwood-7b-q4 with long tail on TokenGeneration.

lee: any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy finished: service/runtime v3.14.0 -> v3.14.1 by @oliver at 2098765300

oliver: I rolled a small patch to the routing logic to prefer lower-cost variants for background tasks — shouldn't affect realtime requests but possible bug. Rolling back now as precaution.

maria: rollback initiated. but we need to triage root cause. jamal, can you paste the slow stack traces and KV cache stats?

jamal: logs snippet: ```
2026-03-15T10:02:10Z runtime[worker-12] WARN token-gen latency=1850ms model=model-redwood-7b-q4 seq=1024 queue_len=18
2026-03-15T10:02:11Z runtime[worker-5] WARN prefix-cache miss key=user:acme-inc:conv-988
``` Cache hit rate dropped from 94% to 63% in the window.

lee: lower cache hit -> more generation work. Could be upstream cache invalidation bug. Any cache purge jobs running?

oliver: There was a maintenance job yesterday cycling prefix-cache when we changed serialization. I thought it was gated but maybe not for this customer due to their custom routing.

maria: immediate mitigations we can apply (short list):
- re-enable sticky routing to cached hosts for acme-inc
- bump concurrency for pool 'us-west-realtime' by +20% (scale up)
- temporarily route acme-inc to fallback model redwood-3b-legacy (lower latency)
- increase request-level circuit breaker sensitivity to drop slow requests earlier
- add rate-limit for heavy realtime endpoints for this customer if they exceed baseline

jamal: I can flip sticky routing and bump pool sizes now. Doing sticky routing -> ```PATCH /routing/customer/acme-inc { "sticky": true, "sticky_ttl_secs": 600 }```

maria: go for it. Also please enable a circuit-breaker rule:
```
circuit_breaker {
  name: "acme-realtime-latency-cb"
  metric: p99_latency_ms
  window: 60s
  threshold: 1200
  action: "short-circuit-to-fallback"
}
```

oliver: I'll push a temporary policy that reroutes to redwood-3b-legacy when CB trips. Also tweaking rate-limit: customer_concurrency_limit=12 -> 8 during the incident.

support-ops: communicating to customer: "We're rolling a temporary routing + fallback model, and increasing capacity; will follow up with RCA once stabilized" :thumbsup:

sre-bot: autoscale request acknowledged for pool us-west-realtime: scale up +3 instances (GPU). ETA ~2m.

jamal: pool scaled. sticky routing enabled. circuit breaker policy in place. applied rate-limit. I see p95 drop to ~220ms after these changes, p99 down to ~540ms in the next 3m.

maria: good. now action items for postmortem / guardrails:
1) Add an SLO guardrail that enforces a per-customer prefix-cache hit-rate alert (if < 80% for 5m -> page).
2) Don't allow prefix-cache maintenance jobs to run with global scope during business hours or for customers with sticky routing enabled.
3) Add automated fallback chaining: if model X p99 > SLO -> route to model X-compat-fallback in same region before scaling up remote regions.
4) Formalize circuit-breaker defaults: window=60s threshold=1.5x SLO p99, action=fallback then throttled retry (exponential backoff).
5) Default customer concurrency caps with emergency overrides: configurable per-customer.

lee: also add observability: per-route token-level latency histogram + early-warning anomaly detector (based on rolling baseline) so we catch p95 shifts before p99 spikes.

oliver: I'll file infra PRs tonight to add the CB default and fallback chaining. Re: maintenance job gating, that's on platform config — i'll add a whitelist for maintenance windows.

maria: support-ops: please ask acme-inc to retry the repro after an hour and share a new trace if they still see issues. We'll include the temp mitigation details in the ticket.

support-ops: done. customer acknowledged.

jamal: follow-up note — root cause hypothesis: maintenance job cleared parts of prefix cache for a subset of hosts, routing change after deploy meant some customers no longer hit the cache-coherent hosts -> large cache misses -> longer generation latency and queueing.

maria: makes sense. long-term mitigation timeline (owner):
- infra (oliver): enforce maintenance gating + add test for cache-coherency routing (2w)
- runtime (jamal): improve KV cache warmup and reduce cold-start penalty (3w)
- observability (lee): add per-customer cache-hit-rate alert and auto-remediation playbook (1w)
- product/sales (support-ops): update SLA language with fallback model clauses and emergency rate-limits (1w)

oliver: adding unit tests for routing + cache affinity today. PR will reference INC-5412.

maria: final communication: incident resolved, postmortem and RCA will be posted in #incidents. Closing thread when PM approves draft. Thanks all. :pray:

support-ops: tagging customer in ticket and marking as mitigated.

sre-bot: incident INC-5412 status -> mitigated (temporary workarounds applied).
